title: Filet crochet shawl
subtitle: A triangular shawl worked in filet mesh with solid block details.
excerpt: Filet crochet alternates open mesh squares with solid block squares to build pictures or geometric patterns into the fabric. This triangular shawl uses a simple diamond grid as its centrepiece worked in lace weight on a 3.5 mm hook.
sourceNotes: Filet crochet as a domestic craft is documented from the 1890s in Weldon's Practical Needlework series (Internet Archive). The open-mesh solid-block grid is the foundational technique of 20th-century filet pattern books. This shaping and chart are original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A grid of open squares (one treble, two chains, skip two stitches) and solid squares (three trebles) worked in rows. Charts show which squares are open and which are filled to create patterns.
A filet square left as a gap: one treble at each edge with a two-chain bridge in the middle.
A filet square filled in with trebles: three trebles worked close together with no chain gap.
Wetting or steaming finished crochet and pinning it to the stated dimensions so lace opens up fully.

crochet.gaugeText: 10 mesh squares x 10 rows = 10 x 10 cm in lace weight with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Triangular shawl, 170 cm wingspan x 80 cm deep at centre back, blocked.

content.text: A filet crochet shawl is a triangular piece 170 cm across the wingspan and 80 cm deep at the centre back. The fabric is a grid of
squares, each one either open or filled in. Open squares let light through; solid squares build up the pattern.
The shawl is worked from the top back neck edge downward, increasing by two
squares per row at each side edge. A diamond grid sits in the centre panel, with
tracing the diamond outline against an open mesh background.

items.name: Lace weight yarn
items.substitutions: A smooth lace or cobweb weight in cotton or silk-cotton blend shows filet patterns sharply.

content.text: 10 mesh squares x 10 rows = 10 x 10 cm in lace weight with a 3.5 mm hook, blocked. Work a 20-square-wide swatch across 15 rows, block it, and measure. The gauge determines the finished width. At 10 squares per 10 cm, the shawl reaches 170 cm at 170 squares wide.
: 1 tr, ch 2, skip 2 sts, 1 tr at the far edge
Ch 7 (counts as 1 open mesh square: 1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr in turning chain). Turn.

Ch 8 (counts as 1 increase open mesh at left edge). Work 1 tr into the ch-4 base of row 1 to close the new increase mesh. Ch 2, skip 2, 1 tr into the last ch. Ch 5. Work 1 tr into the same last ch (increase open mesh at right edge). Turn. (3 open mesh squares.)

Each right-side row increases by one open mesh at each edge using the ch-8 turn-and-fill method. Each wrong-side row mirrors the right side. Work in pattern following the chart: read right-side rows from right to left, wrong-side rows from left to right. The centre diamond appears from Row 15. Work 80 rows total.

Rows 15 to 45: The centre 11 squares of each row trace a diamond outline. On Row 15, the centre square is a solid block. On Row 16, the two squares either side of centre are solid. Continue expanding by two solid squares per row until Row 30 (the widest row of the diamond), then mirror back in to Row 45. All surrounding squares remain open mesh.
Work one row of double crochet around all three edges of the triangle.

by soaking and pinning each corner and several points along each edge. The mesh opens significantly: an unblocked 10 x 10 cm swatch can reach 13 x 13 cm blocked, so pin to the stated 170 x 80 cm rather than working to a smaller target.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Filet mesh shawls have specific issues around counting and edge shaping.

items.cause: Missing the ch-8 turning chain increase method
items.fix: The ch-8 at the start of a right-side row forms one new open mesh and the turning chain for the row. Count it as a mesh square before working across.

items.cause: Reading the chart from the wrong direction on wrong-side rows
items.fix: Mark every wrong-side row on the chart before you start. Read these rows from left to right on the chart so solid blocks fall in the correct columns.
Work all ch-2 bridges over a pencil or crochet hook one size larger to keep them consistent, then remove before the next row.
